title: decouple-serializer-from-affinity-and-introduce-cooperative-serialize-queues
author: Avery Chen
description: Motivation: our telemetry and recent incident traces show a non-trivial CPU-side bottleneck in the request hotpath caused by blocking serialization work that holds thread-affinity (OS-level pinning) and prevents efficient cooperative scheduling between IO, serializer, and runtime workers. This PR separates the concerns: (1) introduce a lightweight cooperative serialization queue that runs on worker threads without requiring permanent thread pinning, (2) decouple the serializer state machine from thread-affinity so short critical sections can opportunistically run on any available worker, and (3) add backpressure signals to the queue which feed into the scheduler to dynamically throttle batch assembly when CPU saturation is detected. Design summary: add runtime/serialize_queue.{h,cpp} implementing a fixed-size ring queue with lock-free handover for small payloads and a CAS-protected overflow path for large messages. Add a SerializerActor that owns transient per-request buffers but is not bound to a specific CPU core; a short move-to-stack and memcpy micro-optimization keeps copies minimal. Thread pool changes: make ThreadPool::pinning optional at task-granularity, introduce ThreadPool::submit_cooperative(task) which participates in the cooperative scheduling loop. KV cache interaction: when a request hits KV cache for a prefix, the cache lookup now signals the serialize queue to short-circuit full marshalling when cached prefix covers >70% of tokens. Rollout strategy: feature-flag guarded, defaults off for Dedicated regions until we run a gated canary. Benchmarks: integration perf runs on our internal perf-lab show median tail (P95) endpoint latency improvement of 9.2% on mixed small/medium requests, median CPU sys-time for request workers fell from 42% to 29% under the same load profile (16 concurrent clients), and end-to-end tokens/sec improved by 12% for continuous-batching workloads due to reduced serialization stalls. Safety and testing: unit tests for the queue and overflow path, stress tests with randomized task yields, and end-to-end perf harness runs included. Compatibility: no API change to external clients. Rollback plan: flip feature flag and revert the small patch in main that wires up the queue. Notes: this is intentionally conservative on the overflow path to avoid introducing GC/alloc churn in the hotpath.

release_notes: Improve CPU-side request throughput by introducing cooperative serialization queues and decoupling serializer state from strict thread-affinity. Expect ~10% tail latency reduction and ~12% token throughput increase for continuous-batching workloads. Rollout gated behind feature flag.
